summary: Completed targeted Cricsheet history API and dashboard regression testing. Persisted dataset reports 1,243 matches and 1,218 tracked outcomes; normalized list responses omit _id and innings; real metrics, attribution, chart/table, safe source link, mobile layout, and live fixture explorer all passed.

minor.issue: Each import uses a new timestamp run_id and replace_one on that unique ID, so repeated imports add metadata documents indefinitely even though match documents are idempotently upserted.

action_items: Consider making ingestion-run metadata idempotent by keying on archive SHA/version (or explicitly retaining bounded run history) and add a repeated-import regression test.
critical_code_review_comments: The match collection is safely upserted by deterministic cricsheet match_id, but ingestion run metadata is keyed by timestamp and will grow on every repeated import.
seed_data_creation: None; used the existing persisted Cricsheet dataset and live fixture feed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: History API and dashboard verified on public URL at desktop/mobile. Re-test ingestion twice and compare cricsheet_ingestion_runs count; no ingestion was executed during this iteration to avoid downloading/replacing the production preview dataset.
rca of the issue: normalize_match creates deterministic cricsheet:<source id> match IDs and replace_one(upsert=True) prevents duplicate match growth. ingest instead creates run_id=datetime.now(...).isoformat() and replaces by that unique value, guaranteeing a new metadata row per invocation.
